players.product: discretes, power MOSFETs and PCIe clock / switch ICs for servers

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results (CFO Brett Whitmire, CEO Gary Yu): revenue was $445.5 million, up 22% from $366.2 million a year earlier and up 10% from $405.5 million in Q1 2026 - the fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit year-over-year growth, with growth across all regions and record global POS. Gross margin was 33.1% versus 31.5% a year ago and 31.8% last quarter (up 160 basis points year over year, credited to earlier cost and operating initiatives). GAAP net income was $46.6 million or $1.00 per diluted share; non-GAAP adjusted net income was $32.5 million or $0.70 per diluted share (versus $0.32 a year ago); EBITDA was $83.5 million or 18.7% of revenue. CEO: growth reflects strengthening overall demand plus expanding content across analog and power solutions in automotive, industrial and AI server-related applications.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 revenue $445.5 million (+22% YoY from $366.2 million, +10% QoQ from $405.5 million); gross margin 33.1% (31.5% a year ago, 31.8% prior quarter); GAAP EPS $1.00; non-GAAP EPS $0.70; EBITDA $83.5 million (18.7%)

quarterly_data.signal: End-market and regional mix (SVP Worldwide Sales and Marketing Emily Yang): Asia was 79% of revenue, Europe 12% and North America 9%. Product revenue: industrial 23%, automotive a record 21%, computing 28%, consumer 17%, communication 11%. Automotive revenue grew 15% sequentially and over 37% year over year on business expansion and share gains; industrial grew 5% sequentially and over 24% year over year; computing - 'our strongest growth driver' on data center, AI server, cloud infrastructure and storage adoption - grew 18% sequentially and 33% year over year; consumer grew almost 10% sequentially and 17% year over year but remained challenged by memory shortage; communication fell 7% sequentially and approximately 3% year over year on soft China smartphone demand, while networking stayed strong on AI infrastructure and enterprise networking investment.
quarterly_data.figure: Asia 79%, Europe 12%, North America 9%; industrial 23%, automotive 21%, computing 28%, consumer 17%, communication 11%; automotive +15% QoQ / over 37% YoY; industrial +5% / over 24%; computing +18% / 33%; consumer almost 10% / 17%; communication -7% / approximately 3% YoY decline

quarterly_data.signal: AI infrastructure content (Emily Yang): AI infrastructure 'is becoming an increasingly important growth driver for Diodes that spans multiple end markets'; in a typical AI infrastructure platform Diodes content attaches to the server motherboard, a power network across the full power life cycle, networking switches, storage and high-speed optical interconnect. Across these combined AI application areas the estimated total content opportunity is approximately $267, versus $109 for AI server platforms, and several new products are scheduled for release over the next few quarters to expand BOM content and socket penetration.
quarterly_data.figure: estimated AI infrastructure content opportunity approximately $267 vs $109 for AI server platforms

quarterly_data.signal: Server timing design wins (Emily Yang): the timing portfolio kept gaining traction as customers transition to next-generation PCI Express architectures; Diodes 'secured multiple strategic server platform design wins for our clock generators and timing solutions', with design activity, customer engagement and backlog trending strong, and new timing products 'are now ramping into the latest AI server platforms'. Rising AI server power density is also driving strong demand for its power distribution, protection, sensing and voltage reference portfolios.

400V / 800V AI power architectures (Emily Yang): 'with the shift towards 400-volt and 800-volt power architectures becoming an important trend in AI-related applications, our power management product and discrete products remain key growth drivers'; the transition supports higher power density, lower distribution losses and more efficient intermediate bus conversion, creating additional content opportunity. Humanoid robotics is an emerging opportunity for discretes, voltage translation and connectivity, and in automotive the move to higher-voltage EV platforms is driving demand for Diodes' power semiconductors and wide band gap solutions.

Q3 2026 guidance (CFO Brett Whitmire, CEO Gary Yu): revenue approximately $510 million, plus or minus 3% - at the midpoint up 30% year over year and 14% sequentially; GAAP gross margin 35%, plus or minus 1% (a 190 basis point sequential improvement as utilization improves); non-GAAP adjusted EPS $1.05, plus or minus $0.10 (a 2.8x year-over-year improvement); full-year 2026 tax rate approximately 18%, plus or minus 3%. Emily Yang expects growth from almost all end markets, 'the majority' driven by AI-related applications especially on the server motherboard side, plus automotive share gains, an industrial recovery and AI networking switches and routers; she sees 'good momentum so far for Q4' and next year 'should be stronger than usual'. The CEO reiterated the three-year goals of $2 billion in annual revenue and over $4 in non-GAAP EPS.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 2026 revenue approximately $510 million +/- 3% (+30% YoY, +14% QoQ at midpoint); GAAP gross margin 35% +/- 1%; non-GAAP EPS $1.05 +/- $0.10; three-year goals $2 billion revenue, over $4 non-GAAP EPS

quarterly_data.signal: Supply and channel (Emily Yang, CFO Brett Whitmire): channel inventory decreased in dollars and weeks again, below the normal range of 11 weeks to 14 weeks, and management sees no double booking; 'the supply disruption I've mentioned on previous calls continues', and with demand so strong 'definitely there are pockets where supply is a little bit constrained'. Total inventory rose to $504.6 million while inventory days fell to approximately 152 from 157; the CFO said the build supports customers, expected growth and 'longer wafer manufacturing lead times'.
quarterly_data.figure: channel inventory below normal 11 to 14 weeks; inventory $504.6 million; inventory days approximately 152 (157 prior quarter)

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity plan (CEO Gary Yu): Diodes expects 'very strong demand this year, and even more so next year' and says growth is not limited by capacity it can bring online. Wafer fabs: utilization keeps improving at GFAB and SPFAB (key customers are starting to use wafers from SPFAB), with migration from 6-inch to 8-inch for more capacity and added capacity from external partners in Korea and Taiwan. About 75% of assembly and test is done internally, with capacity added selectively for advanced packages such as CSP. Production is 'about 50-50' internal versus outsourced. Q2 capital expenditures were $33.6 million or 7.5% of revenue, within the targeted 5% to 9% of revenue range.
quarterly_data.figure: about 75% of assembly and test in-house; production about 50-50 internal vs outsourced; Q2 capex $33.6 million (7.5% of revenue; target 5% to 9%)

quarterly_data.signal: Proposed acquisition of ElevATE Semiconductor (CEO Gary Yu): ElevATE is a fabless semiconductor company developing ICs for automated test equipment (ATE), adding signal chain amplifiers and data converters to Diodes' analog and mixed-signal portfolio. The CEO said the deal is immediately accretive and expected to add approximately $50 million of revenue in the first 12 months post close, with revenue expected to grow at a CAGR of greater than 20% over the next four years and gross margin significantly higher than Diodes' corporate average; combined, Diodes can address an ATE market of at least $1 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $50 million revenue in first 12 months post close; CAGR greater than 20% over four years; addressable market at least $1 billion
